projects.title: Low-Latency Pitching Biomechanics System
projects.experience: NU MIE / Boston Red Sox Capstone Project
projects.overview: Proposed and led a senior capstone project: a portable, low-latency pitching biomechanics capture system
descriptions: Pitched the project to the Red Sox sponsor and capstone advisor, then led a hand-picked team through 8 months of NDA-protected development
The system merges real-time IMU sensor streams with event detection to calculate targeted metrics for player development and injury risk mitigation
IMUs sit in a custom compression sleeve with integrated sensor pockets for repeatable placement, designed to reduce soft-tissue artifact during explosive movement
Built the full software stack: a supplemental streaming source, an ASCII command parser, a sensor calibration procedure, a PyQt desktop interface, and an iOS companion app in Swift
Targeted sub-60-second feedback, with event detection triggering on 97% of test pitches
Rebuilt after graduation into a fully functional end-to-end version with sub-40-second feedback and 100% event detection on the original test set

projects.title: Hall of Fame Pitcher Model
projects.overview: A Generalized Additive Model that predicts Hall of Fame induction from pitching careers
descriptions: Built a Generalized Additive Model (pygam) trained on Hall of Fame voting using the Lahman Baseball Database (1900-2024), correctly predicting zero pitchers elected in the 2026 BBWAA class

Engineered 30+ features, including tensor-product interactions between career timing and counting statistics to contextualize performance across eras, as well as awards voting to quantify non-statistical voter criteria
Benchmarked against an XGBoost classifier, choosing GAMs to model smooth relationships to better reflect how voters evaluate borderline candidates
Published a full technical write-up on Medium covering methodology, feature importance, edge cases, and the Big Hall vs. Small Hall debate

projects.title: Pitching Delivery Classifier
projects.overview: Cluster pitching deliveries into windup, stretch, and slide-step from markerless motion-capture data using Gaussian Mixture Models
descriptions: Proposed an unsupervised approach to classify unrecorded pitching deliveries on a pitch level
Engineered biomechanical features capturing setup geometry and lower-body timing from KinaTrax markerless motion-capture data

Built a per-pitcher Gaussian Mixture Model that selects its own cluster count via a combined BIC and silhouette criterion, then labels clusters as windup, stretch, or slide-step using game-situation context as a ground-truth signal
Validated cluster separation with statistical methods and visualizations

projects.title: 3D Baseball Trajectory Simulation at Fenway Park
projects.overview: A VPython 3D simulation of a batted ball's flight at dimensionally-accurate Fenway Park model
descriptions: Simulated a batted baseball's 3D flight at Fenway Park in VPython, numerically integrating kinematics equations under quadratic drag plus gravity
Adapted a 2D Particle2D class from a computational physics assignment into a custom Particle3D class using VPython vectors for position/velocity state
Compared Euler, RK4, and symplectic Leapfrog integration schemes, verifying energy was conserved to within floating-point round-off in the drag-free case

Grounded physical constants in Dr. Alan Nathan's public Trajectory Calculator, and compared the model's ~401 ft prediction against a Statcast average of 427 ft, attributing the gap to the omission of backspin and Magnus lift

media.caption: 3D trajectory simulation in VPython

projects.title: Torpedo Bat Vibration & Sweet-Spot Model
projects.overview: Computational physics model evaluating the effect of bat mass distribution on performance
descriptions: Modeled a baseball bat as a Timoshenko beam using finite-element analysis to solve its vibration mode shapes and natural frequencies
Extracted real bat width profiles from photographs using OpenCV to drive the model from actual bat geometry
Coupled the model to collision mechanics from Dr. Alan Nathan's work to estimate batted-ball performance versus impact location
Compared a standard bat against a torpedo bat sweet spot, building on Vivienne Pelletier's public work on torpedo-bat vibration modes
Concluded from the model that the torpedo profile offered little meaningful performance advantage over a standard bat

media.caption: Vibration mode shapes from the beam model with each mode's natural frequency
Predicted sweet spot along the barrel: 26.8 in (normal) vs. 26.6 in (torpedo), essentially unchanged

projects.title: Sports Analytics Hackathon Predictive Model
projects.overview: First-place hackathon entry using an XGBoost model to predict batted-ball exit velocity
descriptions: Won 1st place (solo) at the inaugural NU Sports Analytics Hackathon with a winning test MSE of ~120 against a held-out test dataset
Built an XGBoost regression model leveraging features engineered from Statcast pitch-level data to predict exit velocity
Explored unsupervised pitch clustering and a prototype "Stuff+" pitch-quality metric as candidate features
Interpreted the model with SHAP plots and PCA, and ran a feature-selection sweep, reaching R² ≈ 0.37 (MSE ≈ 130) on an internal train/test split

projects.title: Baseball Aerodynamics CFD Study
projects.overview: Ansys Fluent CFD study of a baseball's Magnus lift and turbulent drag
descriptions: Modelled three cases for Ansys Fluent study: 3D steady-state smooth ball, 3D transient smooth ball with a rotating/sliding mesh, and 3D transient seamed ball
Modeled complex geometry in SolidWorks and generated inflation-layer meshes up to ~2.1 million cells
Ran a parameter sweep over various spin rates and pitch speeds
Integrated simulated force components in MATLAB via kinematic equations to reconstruct 3D trajectories using numerical methods
The simulations never fully converged and produced unrealistic movement, which was attributed to compute limits rather than modeling error

media.caption: Smooth-ball domain mesh, with boundary-layer inflation detail (inset)
Seam-resolved case: outer domain mesh and the seamed ball surface (inset)
Velocity contour featuring an asymmetric wake indicating the Magnus effect
Residuals (top) and force history (bottom): continuity plateaus, force never settles

projects.title: Ninja Warrior Obstacle Course
projects.overview: A backyard American Ninja Warrior-style obstacle course packing 11 obstacles into a 9 ft tall by 9 ft by 14 ft footprint, designed and built with my father for strength training, with heavily overengineered joints and load-bearing supports.
descriptions: Designed and built an 11-obstacle American Ninja Warrior course, featuring lache bars, keyhole grasper, cannonball alley, devil steps, ring toss, peg board, and ultimate cliffhanger into a compact 9 ft tall by 9 ft by 14 ft frame
Sized obstacles and spacing around real constraints: user physicality, available space, materials stocked at Lowe's and Habitat ReStore, and fixed budget
Overengineered every joint and hanging obstacle with an excessive safety factor to hold a person's full weight plus dynamic load, using back-of-envelope calculations to validate spans and supports
Repurposed the landing from a fallen storm-damaged treehouse into the course's stair-and-platform section, reducing material cost and waste
